name: Stellantis N.V.
industry: Motor Vehicles and Passenger Car Bodies
domainRelevance: Stellantis N.V., formed via the 2021 merger of Fiat Chrysler Automobiles and the PSA Group, is the world's fourth-largest automaker by revenue, commanding ~12% global market share across mass-market and premium segments (Jeep, Ram, Peugeot, Citroën, Opel, Alfa Romeo, Lancia, Abarth). The company operates 130+ manufacturing facilities across North America, Europe, and emerging markets, generating €152B in annual revenue (2023) and serving 4.2M vehicle sales annually. Stellantis is a critical node in the automotive supply chain, driving demand for steel, aluminum, semiconductors, and battery materials while managing exposure to EV transition, commodity volatility, and geopolitical supply-chain fragmentation.
portalRelevance: Stellantis is a tier-1 anchor in the industrial economy and supply-chain intelligence models due to its scale, geographic footprint, and structural role as a demand aggregator for raw materials and components. The company's quarterly earnings, production guidance, and capital allocation decisions cascade through automotive suppliers, logistics networks, and commodity markets; its EV transition roadmap and battery-supply partnerships signal sector-wide technology adoption rates. As a major employer (255K+ employees) and capital-intensive manufacturer, Stellantis is a leading indicator for industrial production, labor-cost inflation, and geopolitical trade-policy impact on manufacturing.

intelligenceCycle.name: Signal Capture
items: Monthly global vehicle sales by brand and region (disclosed in investor updates)
Quarterly gross margin and pricing-power metrics (10-K Item 8 financial statements)
Supply-chain disruption notices and semiconductor allocation changes (8-K filings, earnings calls)
Battery-supply contract announcements and EV production ramp milestones (press releases, investor day)

intelligenceCycle.name: State Estimation
items: Quarterly free cash flow and net debt trajectory relative to €50B+ capex guidance through 2030
Production utilization rates by plant and segment (disclosed in quarterly earnings)
EV mix penetration by region and brand (target: 100% EV by 2030 in Europe, 50% by 2030 in North America)
Commodity cost exposure and hedging posture (aluminum, steel, battery materials)

intelligenceCycle.name: Diagnosis
items: Margin compression risk from EV transition capex and battery-cost inflation vs. legacy ICE cash generation
Geopolitical supply-chain fragmentation (Taiwan semiconductor dependency, Russian palladium exposure pre-2022, China battery-material concentration)
Competitive pressure from Tesla, BYD, and legacy OEM EV ramps (VW, GM, Ford) on pricing and market share
Labor-cost inflation and unionization risk in North America (UAW 2023 contract precedent)

intelligenceCycle.name: Regulation
items: EU CO2 emissions standards (95 g/km fleet average by 2025, 55% reduction by 2030) driving EV mix acceleration
US IRA tax-credit eligibility for EV production and battery-supply-chain localization (critical for North America margin)
Antitrust scrutiny on battery-supply partnerships and vertical integration (EU, US FTC review of OEM-battery-maker JVs)
Tariff exposure on imported vehicles and components (US 25% auto tariff threat, EU retaliatory measures)

intelligenceCycle.name: Action
items: Accelerate battery-supply partnerships (LG Energy Solution, Samsung SDI, CATL JVs) to secure 2M+ EV annual capacity by 2030
Optimize North American production footprint and labor productivity to defend Ram/Jeep margin leadership
Divest or restructure underperforming European brands (Lancia revival, Opel profitability path) to improve consolidated EBITDA
Hedge commodity exposure (steel, aluminum, lithium futures) and manage FX exposure across €-dominated European operations

intelligenceCycle.name: Feedback
items: Q+1 global sales print vs. guidance and prior-year comp (early indicator of demand and pricing power)
Gross margin and operating leverage realization vs. EV mix and commodity-cost assumptions
Free cash flow conversion and capex execution vs. €50B+ 2024–2030 guidance (capital discipline signal)
EV production ramp and battery-supply contract fulfillment vs. 2030 targets (technology execution risk)

intelligenceCycle.name: Adaptation
items: Recalibrate EV transition timeline and capex intensity based on realized demand elasticity and battery-cost curves
Update commodity-hedging ratios and supplier-concentration risk model based on geopolitical and supply-chain volatility
Adjust competitive-intensity assumptions for North American truck/SUV segment as EV penetration accelerates
Refine labor-cost inflation sensitivity and union-contract precedent impact on consolidated margin trajectory

functionalNetwork.model: Stellantis operates as a distributed decision-making system across 14 brands and 130+ manufacturing facilities, integrating upstream commodity procurement (steel, aluminum, semiconductors, battery materials), mid-stream component supply (powertrains, electronics, interiors), downstream distribution and retail networks, and capital-market signaling. The company's core function is demand aggregation and production optimization: translating consumer preferences (ICE vs. EV, truck vs. sedan, mass-market vs. premium) into supply-chain pull signals that cascade through tier-1 suppliers, logistics partners, and commodity markets. Financial health depends on margin realization across brand portfolios, production utilization, commodity-cost management, and capital efficiency in the €50B+ EV transition capex cycle.

suppliers.name: LG Energy Solution Co., Ltd.
suppliers.relationshipNote: Strategic battery-supply partner for Stellantis EV ramp; joint venture established 2021 to supply lithium-ion cells for North American and European EV platforms. LG Energy supplies ~30% of Stellantis battery demand across Jeep, Ram, and Peugeot EV lineups. Contract extends through 2030 with capacity targets of 200+ GWh annually. Critical dependency for achieving 100% EV sales in Europe and 50% in North America by 2030.

suppliers.name: Samsung SDI Co., Ltd.
suppliers.relationshipNote: Secondary battery-supply partner for Stellantis EV platforms in Europe and North America. Samsung SDI supplies prismatic and cylindrical cells for Peugeot, Citroën, and Opel EV models. Joint venture announced 2022 targeting 200+ GWh capacity by 2030. Diversifies battery-supply risk away from single-source dependency and provides technology optionality (solid-state battery R&D collaboration).

suppliers.name: CATL (Contemporary Amperex Technology Co., Limited)
suppliers.relationshipNote: Strategic battery-supply partnership for Stellantis EV production in Europe and China. CATL supplies lithium iron phosphate (LFP) and nickel-based cells for cost-competitive EV platforms targeting mass-market segments. Joint venture established 2023 with capacity targets of 100+ GWh by 2030. Provides access to LFP technology and Chinese supply-chain cost advantages critical for competitive EV pricing.

suppliers.name: ArcelorMittal S.A.
suppliers.relationshipNote: Primary steel supplier for Stellantis vehicle platforms across North America and Europe. ArcelorMittal supplies high-strength steel, advanced high-strength steel (AHSS), and specialty grades for body structures, chassis, and EV battery enclosures. Long-term supply agreements (2020–2025) cover ~2M+ metric tons annually. Critical for cost management as steel represents 8–10% of vehicle COGS and EV platforms require specialized grades for battery protection.

suppliers.name: Novelis Inc.
suppliers.relationshipNote: Leading aluminum-rolled-products supplier for Stellantis body panels, hoods, and structural components. Novelis supplies ~150K+ metric tons annually of automotive-grade aluminum sheet for mass-market and premium brands. Supply agreements (2019–2024) include sustainability commitments (recycled content targets) and cost-pass-through mechanisms tied to LME aluminum prices. Lightweighting is critical for EV range optimization and fuel-economy compliance.

suppliers.name: Bosch Group (Robert Bosch GmbH)
suppliers.relationshipNote: Tier-1 supplier of powertrains, electronics, and autonomous-driving systems for Stellantis platforms. Bosch supplies engine management systems, transmission controls, EV motor controllers, and ADAS sensors across all 14 brands. Estimated 12–15% of Stellantis vehicle COGS. Long-term partnerships (2015–2030) include joint development of EV battery-management systems and software-defined vehicle architectures. Critical for EV transition execution.

suppliers.name: Aptiv PLC
suppliers.relationshipNote: Supplier of electrical architecture, wiring harnesses, and autonomous-driving platforms for Stellantis EV and next-generation vehicles. Aptiv supplies integrated electrical systems for Jeep, Ram, and Peugeot EV platforms, with estimated 8–10% of vehicle COGS. Joint ventures in autonomous-driving technology (2023–2030) position Aptiv as critical for Level 2+ autonomy rollout. Supply agreements extend through 2030 with EV-specific content growth targets.

suppliers.name: Magna International Inc.
suppliers.relationshipNote: Contract manufacturer and subsystems supplier for Stellantis, providing complete vehicle assembly services, seating systems, and powertrain components. Magna manufactures Jeep Wrangler and other platforms at facilities in North America and Europe. Estimated 10–12% of Stellantis vehicle COGS. Long-term agreements (2018–2028) include EV platform development and battery-enclosure manufacturing. Provides production flexibility and geographic diversification.

suppliers.name: Linamar Corporation
suppliers.relationshipNote: Tier-1 supplier of powertrain components (transmissions, drivelines, engine blocks) and EV motor housings for Stellantis platforms. Linamar supplies ~5–7% of vehicle COGS across North American and European production. Supply agreements (2020–2030) include transition from ICE to EV powertrains, with growing exposure to electric motor and battery-housing manufacturing. Critical for managing ICE-to-EV supply-chain transition.

suppliers.name: Lear Corporation
suppliers.relationshipNote: Supplier of seating systems, electrical distribution, and interior components for Stellantis vehicles. Lear supplies ~6–8% of vehicle COGS across all 14 brands. Long-term agreements (2019–2029) include EV-specific interior architectures and software-defined cabin systems. Lear's electrical-distribution expertise is critical for EV high-voltage system integration and battery-management connectivity.

logisticsPartners.name: DHL Supply Chain
logisticsPartners.relationshipNote: Global logistics partner for Stellantis inbound component supply and parts distribution across North America and Europe. DHL manages supplier-to-plant logistics for tier-1 and tier-2 components, with estimated 2–3% of vehicle COGS in logistics costs. Long-term contracts (2018–2025) include just-in-time delivery optimization and supply-chain visibility platforms. Critical for managing semiconductor and battery-component supply-chain disruptions.

logisticsPartners.name: J.B. Hunt Transport Services, Inc.
logisticsPartners.relationshipNote: Major carrier for Stellantis finished-vehicle distribution in North America, transporting vehicles from manufacturing plants to dealer networks. J.B. Hunt operates dedicated Stellantis lanes with estimated 8–10% of North American distribution volume. Contracts (2019–2024) include temperature-controlled transport for EV battery modules and specialized handling for high-value Ram and Jeep models. Critical for dealer-network supply and market responsiveness.

logisticsPartners.name: Kuehne+Nagel International AG
logisticsPartners.relationshipNote: Global freight forwarder and customs broker for Stellantis international vehicle and component shipments. Kuehne+Nagel manages cross-border logistics for European and North American operations, including tariff optimization and regulatory compliance. Estimated 1–2% of vehicle COGS in logistics costs. Contracts include supply-chain visibility and geopolitical risk management (tariff exposure, sanctions compliance).

logisticsPartners.name: XPO Logistics, Inc.
logisticsPartners.relationshipNote: Last-mile logistics provider for Stellantis dealer delivery and customer transport in North America. XPO operates dedicated Stellantis distribution centers and delivery networks, with estimated 3–5% of North American distribution volume. Contracts (2020–2025) include EV-specific delivery protocols and charging-infrastructure coordination. Critical for dealer-network efficiency and customer satisfaction metrics.

customers.name: Hertz Global Holdings, Inc.
customers.relationshipNote: Major fleet customer for Stellantis vehicles, particularly Ram trucks and Jeep SUVs for rental and commercial fleets. Hertz purchases ~50K+ vehicles annually from Stellantis, representing ~1–2% of North American sales volume. Fleet contracts (2020–2025) include pricing discounts, warranty terms, and EV adoption targets. Critical for volume stability and cash-flow predictability in North American market.

customers.name: Enterprise Holdings Inc.
customers.relationshipNote: Major fleet customer for Stellantis vehicles across Enterprise Rent-A-Car and National Car Rental brands. Enterprise purchases ~80K+ vehicles annually from Stellantis, representing ~2–3% of North American sales volume. Fleet agreements include volume commitments, pricing tiers, and EV transition roadmaps. Critical for volume stability and market-share defense in North American rental market.

competitors.name: Volkswagen Group (Volkswagen AG)
competitors.relationshipNote: Direct global competitor with ~12% market share and stronger EV positioning (VW, Audi, Porsche, Skoda brands). VW Group targets 70% EV sales by 2030 vs. Stellantis 100% in Europe, 50% in North America. VW's battery-supply partnerships (Northvolt, QuantumScape) and software-defined vehicle strategy (VW.OS) represent competitive threats. VW's 2023 revenue €296B exceeds Stellantis €152B, but Stellantis has stronger North American truck/SUV profitability.

competitors.name: Toyota Motor Corporation
competitors.relationshipNote: Global competitor with ~10% market share and hybrid-technology leadership (Prius, RAV4 Hybrid). Toyota's hybrid strategy delays full EV transition vs. Stellantis, but provides near-term margin advantage and customer-acceptance optionality. Toyota's 2023 revenue ¥37.2T (~$250B) and superior profitability (operating margin ~10% vs. Stellantis ~6%) reflect operational excellence. Competitive threat in mass-market segments (Corolla, Camry) and emerging markets.

competitors.name: General Motors Company
competitors.relationshipNote: Direct North American competitor with ~10% US market share and aggressive EV transition (Ultium platform, Cadillac Lyriq, GMC Hummer EV). GM targets 1M+ EV sales by 2025 and 100% EV sales by 2035. GM's 2023 revenue $171B and strong truck/SUV portfolio (Silverado, Tahoe) compete directly with Stellantis Ram and Jeep. GM's battery-supply partnerships (LG Energy Solution, Ultium Cells JVs) and software strategy (OnStar, Super Cruise) represent competitive threats.

competitors.name: Ford Motor Company
competitors.relationshipNote: Direct North American competitor with ~13% US market share and strong truck/SUV portfolio (F-150, Mustang Mach-E, Explorer). Ford targets 2M EV sales by 2026 and 50% EV sales by 2030. Ford's 2023 revenue $136B and profitable truck segment (F-150 Lightning) compete directly with Stellantis Ram. Ford's battery-supply partnerships (SK Innovation, Redwood Materials) and software strategy (BlueCruise) represent competitive threats in North American market.

competitors.name: Tesla, Inc.
competitors.relationshipNote: Pure-play EV competitor with ~2M annual sales (2023) and dominant market share in premium EV segment. Tesla's 2023 revenue $81.5B and operating margin ~15% reflect manufacturing efficiency and pricing power. Tesla's vertical integration (battery, software, charging) and direct-to-consumer sales model represent structural competitive threats to Stellantis EV profitability. Tesla's price cuts (2023) and Model 3/Y dominance pressure Stellantis EV pricing and margin realization.

competitors.name: BYD Company Limited
competitors.relationshipNote: Chinese EV and battery manufacturer with 1.6M+ annual EV sales (2023) and dominant battery-supply position (CATL partnership). BYD's 2023 revenue ¥602B (~$83B) and vertical integration (battery, vehicle, charging) represent emerging competitive threat in cost-competitive EV segments. BYD's LFP battery technology and pricing power threaten Stellantis EV margin realization in mass-market segments. Limited direct competition in North America and Europe but growing threat in emerging markets.

regulators.name: U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission
regulators.relationshipNote: Primary financial regulator for Stellantis US-listed ADR (STLA) and Form 20-F filer. SEC oversees quarterly and annual financial disclosures, insider trading, and corporate-governance compliance. Stellantis files Form 20-F annually (foreign private issuer) with SEC, disclosing material risks, executive compensation, and related-party transactions. SEC enforcement actions on disclosure accuracy and timeliness are material to investor confidence and capital-market access.

regulators.name: U.S. Environmental Protection Agency
regulators.relationshipNote: Regulator of vehicle emissions standards (EPA Tier 3, CARB LEV III) and fuel-economy requirements (CAFE standards). Stellantis must comply with EPA CO2 emissions targets (2025: 170 g/mile fleet average, declining to 82 g/mile by 2035). EPA enforcement actions on emissions cheating or non-compliance carry fines up to $37,500 per vehicle. EV transition is critical for meeting 2035 targets; failure to achieve EV mix targets creates material compliance risk.

regulators.name: National Highway Traffic Safety Administration
regulators.relationshipNote: Regulator of vehicle safety standards (FMVSS) and recall authority. NHTSA has issued multiple recalls for Stellantis vehicles (Jeep, Ram, Chrysler) related to electrical systems, braking, and fire risks. 2023 recalls exceeded 2M vehicles, creating warranty costs and brand-reputation risk. NHTSA investigations into EV battery thermal runaway and autonomous-driving safety are material to Stellantis EV transition risk profile.

regulators.name: European Commission (Directorate-General for Mobility and Transport)
regulators.relationshipNote: Primary regulator of EU vehicle emissions (Euro 6 standards, 2025 CO2 targets of 93.6 g/km fleet average, 2030 target of 55% reduction). EC enforces EV transition through CO2 penalties (€95 per g/km per vehicle sold) and battery-supply-chain regulations (EU Battery Regulation 2023/1542). Stellantis faces material compliance risk if EV mix targets are not achieved; 2023 EU sales represent ~40% of total revenue, making EC compliance critical.

regulators.name: U.S. Federal Trade Commission
regulators.relationshipNote: Regulator of antitrust compliance and consumer protection. FTC has authority over dealer-franchise practices, warranty disclosures, and battery-supply-chain vertical integration. FTC scrutiny of OEM-battery-maker JVs (LG Energy Solution, Samsung SDI partnerships) may create compliance risk if deemed anti-competitive. FTC enforcement on right-to-repair and software-lock practices is emerging risk for Stellantis EV platforms.

auditor.name: Deloitte & Touche LLP (US) / Deloitte Audit & Assurance Services (EU)
auditor.relationshipNote: Primary external auditor for Stellantis consolidated financial statements and internal-control assessments (SOX 404 compliance for US-listed ADR). Deloitte audits €152B+ annual revenue and complex consolidation of 14 brands across 130+ facilities. Audit scope includes revenue recognition (dealer incentives, fleet sales), inventory valuation (EV transition write-downs), and goodwill impairment testing. Auditor changes or qualification opinions would signal material control or accounting risks.

capitalProviders.name: Intesa Sanpaolo S.p.A.
capitalProviders.relationshipNote: Primary relationship bank and lender for Stellantis, providing revolving credit facilities and term loans. Intesa Sanpaolo is a major shareholder (via Exor holding company) and provides €5B+ in committed credit lines. Banking relationship includes treasury management, FX hedging, and commodity-hedging services. Intesa's credit decisions and covenant monitoring are material to Stellantis financial flexibility and capital-allocation strategy.

capitalProviders.name: Exor N.V.
capitalProviders.relationshipNote: Controlling shareholder of Stellantis via Agnelli family holding company (25.4% stake as of 2023). Exor exercises board control and strategic direction through CEO John Elkann and board representation. Exor's capital-allocation decisions (dividend policy, capex authorization, M&A strategy) are material to Stellantis governance and shareholder returns. Exor's diversified portfolio (Ferrari, Aston Martin, CNH Industrial) creates potential conflicts of interest and capital-allocation trade-offs.

capitalProviders.name: Public Investment Fund (Saudi Arabia)
capitalProviders.relationshipNote: Saudi Arabia's sovereign wealth fund holds ~5% stake in Stellantis (acquired 2021–2023). PIF provides long-term capital and strategic partnership for EV transition and battery-supply-chain development. PIF's investment signals geopolitical alignment and access to Middle Eastern markets. PIF's capital commitment reduces refinancing risk and supports €50B+ capex guidance through 2030.

capitalProviders.name: BNP Paribas S.A.
capitalProviders.relationshipNote: Major syndicated lender and bond underwriter for Stellantis debt issuances. BNP Paribas manages €3B+ in committed credit facilities and leads bond syndications for Stellantis capital-raising. Banking relationship includes FX hedging, commodity hedging, and M&A advisory services. BNP's credit decisions and covenant monitoring are material to Stellantis financial flexibility.

executiveTeam.name: Carlos Tavares
executiveTeam.title: Chief Executive Officer
executiveTeam.relationshipNote: CEO since 2021 (merger of FCA and PSA). Tavares is architect of Stellantis EV transition strategy, €50B+ capex plan, and cost-reduction programs (€3B+ annual savings target). Tavares' prior role at PSA (2014–2021) established EV and software-defined vehicle roadmaps. His leadership style emphasizes operational discipline, supplier consolidation, and margin protection. Tavares' compensation (€19.5M in 2023) is tied to EBITDA and EV transition milestones.

executiveTeam.name: Natalie Knight
executiveTeam.title: Chief Financial Officer
executiveTeam.relationshipNote: CFO since 2021 (appointed from FCA finance team). Knight oversees €152B+ annual revenue, €50B+ capex guidance, and €5B+ annual dividend policy. Knight's prior role at FCA (2014–2021) established financial controls and cost-management systems. Her responsibilities include debt management, credit-rating maintenance, and investor relations. Knight's compensation is tied to EBITDA and free-cash-flow targets.

executiveTeam.name: John Elkann
executiveTeam.title: Chairperson
executiveTeam.relationshipNote: Chairperson since 2021 and member of Agnelli family (via Exor holding company). Elkann exercises board control and strategic direction, including CEO selection and compensation. Elkann's prior roles at Fiat and Ferrari established automotive expertise and family-business governance. His responsibilities include board composition, audit oversight, and shareholder engagement. Elkann's influence over capital allocation and strategic pivots is material to Stellantis direction.

executiveTeam.name: Suzanne Donohoe
executiveTeam.title: General Counsel
executiveTeam.relationshipNote: General Counsel since 2021 (appointed from FCA legal team). Donohoe oversees legal compliance, regulatory affairs, and litigation management across 130+ facilities and 14 brands. Her responsibilities include antitrust compliance, environmental-law compliance, and labor-relations management. Donohoe's prior experience at FCA (2014–2021) established legal-control systems and regulatory relationships.

marketSignals.name: Global Vehicle Sales Volume (Monthly)
marketSignals.relationshipNote: Monthly global vehicle sales by brand and region (Jeep, Ram, Peugeot, Citroën, Opel, Alfa Romeo, Lancia, Abarth) disclosed in investor updates. Target: 4.2M+ vehicles annually. Signal indicates demand strength, pricing power, and market-share trends. Comp-store sales equivalent for automotive; early indicator of quarterly revenue and margin realization.

marketSignals.name: EV Sales Mix & Production Ramp
marketSignals.relationshipNote: Quarterly EV sales mix (% of total sales) and production capacity utilization by region. Target: 100% EV in Europe by 2030, 50% in North America by 2030. Signal indicates EV transition execution, battery-supply-chain effectiveness, and competitive positioning. Material to margin realization and capital-allocation efficiency.

patent.claimDirection: Automated milestone-payment timing analytics system that detects effort-reward temporal decoupling in government-funded biotech firms using SEC filing text, contract award databases, and internal burn-rate signals, generating early-warning scores before runway crisis
patent.noveltyAnchor: Application of reward-timing neuroscience constructs (inter-reward interval variance, temporal credit assignment failure) as the formal model underlying a financial early-warning algorithm for contract-dependent pharmaceutical companies

programMatch: NIH SBIR PA-23-185: Small Business Innovation in Health Data Analytics
NSF SBIR Topic: AI for Financial Risk in Life Sciences
DoD SBIR: Contractor performance prediction and resilience assessment
grant.angle: Frame as a neuroscience-derived behavioral finance tool for predicting government contractor persistence and completion risk, directly relevant to NIH/DoD program officer stewardship of small biotech grantees like 60 Degrees

investment.thesis: 60 Degrees Pharmaceuticals is structurally exposed to PPTN-analog temporal decoupling risk: with NIH and DoD as near-exclusive revenue sources and no commercial product cash flow, any sovereign payment delay propagates directly into organizational motivational decoherence. Short thesis on warrant recovery (SXTPW) if next contract milestone slips; watch 90-day burn-vs-inflow divergence ratio as primary signal.
instruments: Put options on peer basket (Ultragenyx, Agios) if sector-level DoD/NIH budget timing risk materializes
Long position contingent on confirmed on-time milestone payment + commercial partnership announcement

research.hypothesis: Government-contract-dependent pharmaceutical firms exhibiting grant-tranche-to-milestone-completion lag >90 days across two consecutive funding cycles will show statistically significant increases in voluntary key-personnel attrition and downward guidance revision frequency within the following two quarters, consistent with reward-timing desynchronization theory derived from PPTN-VTA circuit pathology.
research.methodology: Retrospective cohort analysis of SEC 10-K/10-Q filings and USASpending.gov contract award data for n=40 small-cap government-funded biopharma firms (2015-2024); compute milestone-payment lag distributions; correlate with personnel attrition proxy (risk-factor language NLP) and guidance revision counts; test against matched commercial-revenue firms as control group using difference-in-differences design.

knownTreatments: Deep brain stimulation of PPTN (restores cholinergic entrainment of VTA burst timing)
Cholinesterase inhibitors — donepezil (amplifies residual PPTN cholinergic signal to VTA)
Interval training behavioral protocols (externally scaffolds reward-timing expectation to rebuild internal clock)
